To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

patterns of discharge in primary somatosenory cortex cannot be used as reliable indicators of sensory inputs to these neurons because discharge patterns are so strongly influenced, and sometimes determined, by intrinsic membrane properties.

patterns of discharge in cerebral cortical neurons are strongly influenced by intrinsic ionic conductances, and that these patterns of discharge are not reliable indicators of the source and modaility of sensory inputs to these neurons.

intrinsic patterns of discharge in neurons of primary somatosensors cortex are determined by intrinsic membrane properties of the neuron, and that these intrinsic properties are similar in intact cortex of several species and in slices of cerebral cortex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of sensory coding by neurons in the cerebral cortex.
the neural basis for the somatosensory representation in the cerebral cortex.
the role of thalamocortically evoked postsynaptic potentials and intrinsic membrane properties in determining patterns of neuronal discharge in primary somatic sensory cortex of raccoon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the intrinsic membrane properties of neurons in cerebral cortex are very similar across species and preparation, and these properties are a major determinant of discharge patterns of cortical neurons in response to synaptic inputs.
intrinsic discharge patterns in cerebral cortex are not a reliable indicator of the source or modality of sensory inputs.
the intrinsic discharge patterns are a general property for the cortical neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the patterns of neural discharge are strongly influenced by intrinsic properties of neurons and are not reliable estimates of the source and modali
patterns of neural discharge are strongly influenced by intrinsic properties of neurons in primary sensory cortices.
the patterns of discharge of neurons in primary sensory cortex are determined both by synaptic inputs and intrinsic membrane properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intrinsic discharge patterns of cortical neurons are not reliable indicators of the source of their inputs.
the discharge patterns of cortical neurons are not necessarily an accurate reflection of the type of sensory input they are receiving.

intrinsic membrane properties are an essential component in determining patterns of neuronal discharge in primary somotosensory cortex and must be taken into account when determining the nature of the inputs to these neurons.
